To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the empirical Bayes ( EB ) pairwise FST estimator performs well in detecting fine‐scale population structures, and the EB estimators for GST, D and G’ST can be used to detect environmental factors causing population structures.

EBFST is the best estimator for population differentiation when FST is high (e.g. FST≤0.03) and that the EB estimators are useful tools for detecting environmental factors causing population structure.

the EB estimators are useful for detecting fine‐scale genetic population structure in high‐gene flow species, and that the environmental factors affecting the fine‐scale genetic structure can be detected using these estimators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method to estimate fine‐scale population structures in high gene flow populations.
the development of a new empirical Bayes estimator of fine‐scale genetic structure in high gene‐flow populations.
the performance of the EB estimators of pairwise FST, GST and D under various conditions and with real data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the presence of high gene flow, the EBFST is a reliable estimator, and that GST_NC and θ_FWC are reliable alternatives.
EBFST is the best estimator for microsatellite markers and θWC_F is the best for SNPs.
the EBFST is the best estimator for FST in high gene flow populations when the number of locis is less than 1000.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the empirical Bayes estimator of FST is the best estimator for high gene flow species, but the finite sample correction should be applied for θWC when the number of locuses is less than 1000.
EBFST is the best estimator for FST in terms of precision, but the bias of the estimator is greater than those for θWC_F and GST_NC when the number of locis is large.
the EB estimators perform well in detecting population structure, but their performance depends on the number of locuses and the magnitude of FST.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EB estimators are useful for detecting population structure in species with high gene flow.

the EB estimators of FST, G' _{ST}, and D are more accurate and precise than GST, GST_NC, θWC, and θWC_F, and thus are useful for detecting population structure and for identifying factors that cause population structure in high‐gene‐flow species.
EB estimation of FST can be a useful tool for detecting population structure in species with high gene flow.
